name: Disorder of Glycosphingolipid and Glycosylphosphatidylinositol Anchor Glycosylation
aliases: Glycosphingolipid and GPI Anchor Glycosylation Defect
Congenital Glycosylation Disorder of GPI Anchors

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Glycosphingolipid and GPI Anchor Glycosylation Disorders

criteria.description: Abnormal glycosphingolipid and GPI anchor glycosylation profile detected by biochemical assays
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in glycosphingolipid or GPI anchor biosynthesis
Presence of characteristic neurological and systemic clinical features consistent with glycosylation defects
Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase or abnormal flow cytometry for GPI-anchored proteins

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of abnormal biochemical glycosylation profile plus pathogenic genetic variants and compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of biochemical, genetic, and clinical data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

searchTerms: low muscle tone with delayed development

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase due to defective GPI anchor biosynthesis
searchTerms: high alkaline phosphatase due to cell membrane defects
elevated enzyme from protein anchor issues

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment ranging from mild to severe
Dysmorphic facial features including broad nasal bridge and hypertelorism
searchTerms: wide nose bridge and widely spaced eyes
distinct facial features with broad nose and large eye spacing
unusual facial shape with wide nose and eyes

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties
searchTerms: failure to gain weight with eating difficulties
inadequate growth due to feeding issues

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness with delayed motor milestones
searchTerms: slow motor development and weak muscles
repeated infections due to weak immunity

occasional.symptomName: Ocular abnormalities including strabismus and nystagmus
searchTerms: eye movement problems like crossed eyes and shaking
dry, rough skin resembling fish scales

laboratory: Abnormal glycosphingolipid and GPI anchor glycosylation profiles
Flow cytometry showing reduced GPI-anchored proteins on blood cells
imaging: Brain MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
Skeletal X-rays revealing scoliosis or other bone abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in glycosphingolipid or GPI anchor biosynthesis pathways (e.g., PIGA, PIGV, PIGT)
other: Electroencephalogram abnormalities consistent with epileptic encephalopathy

distinguishingFeatures: Abnormal N-glycosylation rather than GPI anchor defects
Distinct biochemical profiles on transferrin isoelectric focusing
Specific flow cytometry patterns of GPI-anchored proteins

redFlags: Early onset hypotonia with developmental delay
Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase without liver disease
references: Ng BG, Freeze HH. Disorders of glycosylation: classification and diagnosis. Curr Opin Pediatr. 2018;30(6):740-750.
Kinoshita T. Biosynthesis and deficiencies of glycosylphosphatidylinositol. Proc Jpn Acad Ser B Phys Biol Sci. 2020;96(4):131-143.
